product_advancement_rate.definition: eligible independent product projects materially advanced by the current orchestrator run divided by independent product projects explicitly proven ELIGIBLE in the run
product_advancement_rate.unknown_policy: do not include UNKNOWN or NO_SAFE_ELIGIBLE_WORK projects in the denominator

portfolio_kpis.rework_source: explicit current-run rework evidence fields interpreted by project_orchestrator.throughput_guard.compute_rework_kpis

durable_flow_telemetry.recording_rule: Record evidenced state transitions at the point they occur, then append exactly one snapshot for the run. Reports query the durable ledger and never reconstruct missing transitions after the fact.
durable_flow_telemetry.authority_rule: Existing KPI definitions and targets remain authoritative. Flow telemetry supplies durable measurements and must not silently redefine first_pass_preflight_rate or any other established target.
durable_flow_telemetry.unknown_policy: Missing transition pairs remain UNKNOWN; absence of an event is never interpreted as a successful transition.
durable_flow_telemetry.scope_rule: Control-plane events may be retained for auditability but are excluded from product-flow health metrics.

scope: each of the three independent product projects
each of the five product repositories
portfolio_kpis.bottleneck_rule: Rank only currently eligible projects and only when the measured-evidence sufficiency rules of project_orchestrator.throughput_optimizer are satisfied. Missing projects remain visible as INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
portfolio_kpis.unknown_policy: UNKNOWN and INSUFFICIENT_DATA are explicit; neither is converted to zero or omitted from the scorecard.
forbidden: predicted time saved without measured evidence
using a KPI or bottleneck rank to override P0-P4 priority, Product Reality, ownership, preflight, CI, review, or product authority

advancement_attribution.rule: Only concrete engineering actions actually performed by the current orchestrator run count toward projects_materially_advanced, product_advancement_rate, or throughput_floor_met.
advancement_attribution.external_rule: Jeremy/manual merges, CI completions, bot actions, and other state changes observed during the run must be reported under external_state_changes and never claimed as this run's output.
advancement_attribution.continuation_rule: If an external action finishes the previously highest-priority item before or during the run, re-triage immediately and continue to the next eligible product action rather than ending the run on the external completion.

learning_evolution.unknown_policy: UNKNOWN is preferred to invented evidence

rules: orchestrator-only control-plane work never counts as product advancement
only current-run ORCHESTRATOR product actions satisfy the throughput floor
Jeremy/manual merges and external state changes are visible but do not count as current-run product advancement
eligible projects without orchestrator advancement require a concrete reason and exact next gate
Jeremy-help opportunities are reported even when they are not blockers
executive status must reflect missed repository inspection or throughput-floor violations
portfolio KPI history is evidence-derived and missing evidence stays visible
record PR/CI/branch/issue transitions once in the durable KPI ledger and finalize one snapshot per run
24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day flow reports come from recorded events, never retroactive inference
bottleneck ranking is advisory and never becomes merge or scheduling authority
